title: fact or fiction?
aim: Fact or fiction?: hoaxes, documentaries, the news and fake friends.
objectives: Talk about past plans and intentions

lessons.title: Hoax!

grammar.title: Past plans and intentions
grammar.shortAr: was/were going to وmeant to وplanned to لخطط سابقة لم تتحقق.
points: was/were going to + infinitive: a plan that did not happen
planned to, hoped to, was planning to are alternatives
didn't mean to = something done by accident
table: They were going to visit the museum, but it was closed.
I planned to visit last week, but I couldn't.
I meant to introduce you to Xavier, but he left.
She didn't mean to cause trouble.
exceptions: intended to is more formal than meant to.

vocab.example: We saw a film about a hoax.
He deceived everyone with his scheme.
They pretended to be other people.
They lived a lie for years.
In the end they came clean.

reading.summary: A story about a hoax: people pretended to be others, lived a lie and finally came clean.

listening.summary: Silent consonants: scheme, doubt, sign, answer, would, listen.

video.summary: People say if they prefer true stories or fiction.

speaking: Retell the story of a hoax.
writing: Write a short news report about a hoax.

lessons.title: Documentary

grammar.title: Indirect and negative questions
grammar.shortAr: السؤال غير المباشر بترتيب إيجابي، والسؤال المنفي للتأكد أو الدهشة.
points: After Could you tell me / Do you know, use affirmative word order
Negative questions check information, show surprise or persuade
Answer a negative question with a short sentence if needed
table: Could you tell me where I have to go?
Do you know who the film-maker is?
exceptions: Not: 'Could you tell me where do I have to go?'.

vocab.example: Shoot more film than you need.
Do you want to add a soundtrack?

listening.summary: Podcast: Amy and Dave discuss two favourite documentaries.

speaking: Present a pitch for a documentary.
writing: Write a review of a documentary.

practice.q: Could you tell me where ___ a taxi rank?
___ you think we should take a taxi?

grammar.title: How to … talk about the news
grammar.shortAr: عبارات لبدء الخبر وتلخيصه بـ basically/apparently والتعليق عليه.
points: Start: Have you heard about...? / Did you hear the news about...?
Summarise: So, basically,... / Apparently,... / It seems that...
React: Really? / That's a relief. / That sounds scary.
table: Did you hear the news about the taxi driver?
So, basically, what happened was she was in a taxi.
Apparently, he drove into the canal.

listening.summary: Five short conversations about news stories.

practice.q: ___, what happened was the driver got lost.

lessons.title: Fake friends

grammar.title: Review: questions and reactions in conversation
grammar.shortAr: مراجعة أسئلة المتابعة وتعابير الدهشة في الحديث مع صديق.
points: Follow-up questions keep a conversation going
Negative questions and 'I thought...' show surprise
table: How long is it since we've seen each other?
I thought you were living in New Zealand.
Do you still see Rob at all?

listening.summary: Nikolas and Jade catch up after years apart.

video.summary: Programme 'Ordinary Lies': an encounter between old acquaintances.

writing: Write a personal email to an old friend.
